title: Restriction and finite-field transport of coefficient dual models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the completed coefficient sheaf $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and the integral, raw scalar-localized rational, and common-stage coefficient categories and internal Hom operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $K$ in the rational constructible domain for which the specified internal Hom into the unit is defined, put $H_E(K)=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,E_X)$. For any coefficient-site object $U$, restriction to $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ has a natural comparison
$$H_E(K)|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{E,U}(K|_U),$$
where the right hand side is the scalar localization of ambient ringed-site internal Hom for $R_E|_U$. These comparisons respect successive restrictions and the unit; $H_{E,U}(E_U)\cong E_U$. If $F$ is a degree-zero module object with a displayed retraction from $E_U^{\oplus m}$ in the localized category, the maps $H_{E,U}(p),H_{E,U}(i)$ exhibit $H_{E,U}(F)$ as a retract of $E_U^{\oplus m}$. For a finite extension $E\subset L$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, let $F_{E,L}=-\otimes_E L$ be the specified scalar extension. On the domains where these Homs are defined the coefficient comparison gives
$$F_{E,L}H_E(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_L(F_{E,L}K).$$
If on a coefficient-site cover $H_E(K)$ has bounded complex models $D_U$ whose terms are actual localized retracts of finite sums of $E_U$, the extended models $F_{E,L}(D_U)$ have the same degree bounds and terms retracting from the corresponding sums of $L_U$, and represent $H_L(F_{E,L}K)$ on that cover. Scalar extension carries each finite stupid-tail triangle and its comparison maps to the corresponding triangle for the extended models. The Hom, unit, restriction and scalar comparisons are natural and compatible with towers of coefficient fields. In the common-stage category the dual of $(E,K)$ is therefore represented by $(E,H_E(K))$, and these models and their extensions represent that same common-stage dual, independently of a further common finite extension. No separatedness condition on $X$, uniform bound over the cover, or lifting of rational retractions to integral ones is assumed.

proof.text: Work with the chosen small site and put $R=R_E$. The ambient restriction theorem applied to $(K,R)$ gives $R\mathcal Hom_R(K,R)|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{R|_U}(K|_U,R|_U)$, natural in $K$ and compatible with relocalization. Restriction is exact on module sheaves, so it also restricts representatives and the coefficient unit. Now scalar-localize this isomorphism and its inverse. For an integral arrow $a$ and scalar $c\in E$, both routes in its naturality square are the integral routes multiplied by $c$, since the rational Hom and restriction act linearly on arrows. Addition gives the assertion for every localized arrow. The successive-restriction equations similarly remain equalities after localization. This proves the first comparison on exactly the stated Hom domain, without imposing constructibility on a resolution or on every intermediate ambient object.

source.place: Tag 08JB, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U; rational arrow formulas in the operation definition.

proof.text: On a slice put $A=R|_U$ and choose a K-injective representative $A[0]\to I$ as in the definition of derived internal Hom. Evaluation at $1$ identifies $\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(A[0],I)$ with $I$, with the same differential. For $A^{\oplus m}[0]$ the identification is $\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(A^{\oplus m}[0],I)=I^{\oplus m}$, by evaluating at the $m$ standard generators; the inverse sends $(y_j)$ to $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_jy_j$. The direct sum of the $m$ augmentations $A[0]\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its cycles, boundaries and quotient are the finite direct sums of those of the augmentation. Thus after scalar localization $H_{E,U}(E_U)=E_U$ and $H_{E,U}(E_U^{\oplus m})\cong E_U^{\oplus m}$. These identifications respect restriction because evaluation at each standard generator does. For $m=0$ all complexes and maps are zero.

source.place: Tag 08J7, construction of internal Hom by a K-injective target; evaluation at the standard generators.

proof.text: Write the displayed localized retraction as $i:F\to E_U^{\oplus m}$, $p:E_U^{\oplus m}\to F$ with $pi=1_F$. Contravariance gives maps $H(p):H(F)\to H(E_U^{\oplus m})$ and $H(i):H(E_U^{\oplus m})\to H(F)$ whose composite is $H(i)H(p)=H(pi)=1_{H(F)}$. Using Step 2 identifies the middle object with $E_U^{\oplus m}$. This proves the required retract directly in the localized category. In particular, if $i=\sum a_j\otimes c_j$ and $p=\sum b_k\otimes e_k$, the same equality follows by expanding the two finite sums and the bilinear composition law; it never requires integral arrows satisfying $pi=1$.

source.place: Rational-level internal-Hom arrow formulas and raw localized composition; direct retract calculation.

proof.text: Apply the integral scalar-comparison theorem to $M=K$, $N=R_E$ and the identity scheme morphism. Its natural internal-Hom isomorphism, followed by rationalization and the coefficient-unit identification, is $F_{E,L}H_E(K)\cong H_L(F_{E,L}K)$. The integral representatives of $K$ and its Hom are in the stipulated domain, so this application does not infer constructibility of an arbitrary ambient Hom. For clarity about the specified scalar functor, the completed coefficient comparison says that $S=R_L$ is finite free over $R$ and that its ordinary derived change of rings agrees naturally with completed scalar extension on complete objects. The unit identification is multiplication $R\otimes_RS\to S$. On a slice use $R|_U\to S|_U$: a finite free basis restricts, so the ambient finite-free Hom base-change theorem applies to arbitrary slice inputs. The ordinary tensor restriction map sends $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes s$; applying it to representatives identifies restriction of the scalar functor with this slice functor. The ambient Hom map is characterized as the transpose of extended evaluation. Slice restriction preserves evaluation and transposes by the slice evaluation-transpose theorem. Hence restricting that defining pairing gives the same pairing for the restricted objects: on tensor generators both scalar/restriction routes send $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes s$. Their transposes are therefore equal. This proves compatibility of these comparisons with restriction, rather than merely the existence of two unrelated isomorphisms.

source.place: Integral scalar comparison specialized to Hom into the unit; finite-free ordinary scalar comparison; Tag 08J9 and ordinary slice tensor restriction.

proof.text: The preceding scalar functor can be computed termwise on every ambient complex on the slice. Indeed $S|_U\cong(R|_U)^{\oplus d}$ as module sheaves. After forgetting the $S|_U$ action, tensoring a module or map is its $d$-fold direct sum: $x\otimes\sum_j a_je_j\mapsto(a_jx)_j$. Kernels and cokernels of these finite sums are computed componentwise, so this additive functor is exact. The exact-functor derived-factorization theorem therefore identifies its derived functor with termwise tensor on every complex, naturally also on derived maps. Its value on a K-flat resolution agrees with derived change of rings, which is computed by that resolution; hence this is the same ordinary functor used in Step 4. Localize its arrow formulas to define the same termwise computation on rational arrows. If a bounded model was supplied as a complex in the raw localized module category, the bounded localized-complex lifting assertion supplies an actual complex with the same support and a localized chain isomorphism to it. Applying the termwise functor to that isomorphism gives the identical localized model computation; no retraction is lifted.

source.place: Finite-free scalar comparison; exact functors on complexes; bounded localized-complex lifting clause of the signed dual presentation.

proof.text: For each cover member choose the given model isomorphism $Q(D_U)\cong H_E(K)|_U$, where $Q$ denotes its realization in the ambient scalar-localized derived category. Apply the functor from Step 5, then Step 4 and Step 1, to obtain $Q(F_{E,L}D_U)\cong H_L(F_{E,L}K)|_U$. If $D_U^r=0$ outside $[a_U,b_U]$, termwise tensor is still zero there. For its displayed term retraction $p_ri_r=1$, functoriality gives $F(p_r)F(i_r)=1$, and the middle object is $L_U^{\oplus m_r}$: multiplication identifies $E_U\otimes_EL$ with $L_U$ and tensor distributes over the finite sum. These are the required actual retractions in the localized category. The argument is performed separately for each $U$, so neither its interval nor its ranks must be uniformly bounded over the cover.

source.place: Local dual model sentence: apply the preceding comparisons to each supplied bounded model.

proof.text: For an actual bounded model $D$, set $D_{\ge c}$ equal to $D$ in degrees at least $c$, zero below. The sequence $0\to D_{\ge c+1}\xrightarrow{i}D_{\ge c}\xrightarrow{p}D^c[-c]\to0$ is split in every degree: in degree $c$ it is $0\to0\to D^c\xrightarrow{1}D^c\to0$ (splitting $r^c=0$, $s^c=1$), above $c$ it is $0\to D^r\xrightarrow{1}D^r\to0\to0$ ($r^r=1$, $s^r=0$), and below $c$ it is zero. The complex short-exact-sequence theorem gives the natural distinguished tail triangle with connecting arrow $\delta$. By the degreewise-split connecting-morphism lemma the splitting defines a chain map $b:D^c[-c]\to D_{\ge c+1}[1]$, $b^k=r^{k+1}d^ks^k$; here its only nonzero component is $b^c=d_D^c:D^c\to D^{c+1}$. The split boundary comparison says $\delta=Q(b)$ after the canonical shift comparison of $Q$. Let $F$ be termwise extension, exact by Step 5. Applied to the sequence and its splitting it gives the tail sequence $0\to(FD)_{\ge c+1}\to(FD)_{\ge c}\to(FD)^c[-c]\to0$ of the extended model with splitting $F(r),F(s)$, the same identity/zero maps, since $F$ is additive and $C(F)$ commutes with the shift by the identity $\tau$. Hence its split boundary is $C(F)(b)$, whose only nonzero component is $F(d_D^c)=d_{FD}^c$, and its connecting arrow is $\delta'=Q(C(F)b)$ by the same two lemmas. The natural isomorphism $\varphi$ of the derived-factorization theorem, applied to the chain maps $i,p,b$ and combined with its shift compatibility (2) for $b$, gives $\varphi\circ F_D(Q i)=Q(C(F)i)\circ\varphi$, likewise for $p$, and $\varphi[1]\circ\sigma\circ F_D(\delta)=\delta'\circ\varphi$. So $\varphi$ is an isomorphism from the image of the tail triangle to the tail triangle of $FD$, compatible with every comparison square. Exact scalar localization carries these equalities and triangles to the localized categories. A localized chain isomorphism from Step 5 transports these equations for a localized model too.

source.place: Tag 0152, derived.tex, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor (canonical connecting map); degreewise split boundary with the shift convention of Tag 011G (homology.tex, homology-definition-shift-cochain).

proof.text: The integral operation comparisons are natural, are identities for $E=L$, and satisfy their coefficient-tower equation. Localizing those equations preserves them: for $E\subset L\subset M$, expanding any finite sum of fraction arrows multiplies their coefficients in $M$ on either route. The canonical scalar composition isomorphisms therefore identify successive extensions of our Hom comparisons and models with direct extension. Unit maps and the slice tensor identifications use multiplication and the same local tensors; further restriction changes none of their formulas. Finally the common-stage Hom of $(E,K)$ into the unit is, by its definition, $(E,H_E(K))$. At any larger finite field its representative is identified with $(L,H_L(F_{E,L}K))$ by Step 4. Their inverse isomorphisms represent inverse common-stage arrows, and the tower equation identifies these arrows after every further extension. Equality of common-stage representatives is precisely equality after a common finite extension. This proves independence of the larger field, also for the bounded models and tail maps already transported, and supplies the claimed naturality. No idempotent completion or integral splitting has entered.
